## Why this exists

This process answers two failures that recur wherever several AI sessions work one repository at once. Case studies:
<https://github.com/Revelation-Hosting/claude-role-lanes/blob/main/docs/why.md>.

**1. A global decision made from local information.** Sessions working in parallel each find something real. Each
reasons, correctly from what it can see, that its find belongs in the release in flight. Together they turn a small
release into a large one that nobody planned. Nobody is careless. **Milestone assignment is a global decision**, and
each session makes it alone.

**2. A verification of the wrong artifact.** A fix is reported "verified" on the strength of a green build and a
code-path argument, while the test ran against a binary that does not contain the fix. **A green build is not
verification.**

## The roles

Definitions live in `.claude/agents/*.md`. Keep them committed to git, so they are identical on every machine.

**How a session adopts one depends on where it starts:**

| Where | How | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal | `claude --agent discovery` | **Strongest.** Replaces the system prompt; persists across resume. |
| Claude Desktop | CLAUDE.md's first-turn question -> pick a role -> the session reads `.claude/agents/<role>.md` and treats it as binding | **Workable.** Desktop has no role picker. |
| Any session | `@discovery` or the Agent tool | **Scoped.** Runs the role as a subagent for one task, then returns. Does *not* adopt the role for the session. |

Saying *"you are a discovery agent"* in a prompt does **nothing**: it never loads the file. That is worse than not
trying, because it looks like it worked.

Do **not** set `"agent"` in `.claude/settings.json`. It pins one role onto every session in the repo, which is the
opposite of choosing per session.

**This is why the hard rules live in CLAUDE.md, not only in the role files.** CLAUDE.md loads in every session
automatically. The role files are the full definitions; CLAUDE.md is the part that always arrives.

| | **Discovery** | **Development** | **Release** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owns | issues, milestone scope, impact | code, PRs, `{{branches.queue}}` | promotion, prod |
| Runbook | Context, invariants, hazards, gates | the concrete steps | the {{release.record_name}} |
| Writes code | **no** | yes | **no** |
| Assigns milestones | **yes - the only role that does** | **no** | **no** |
| Ends at | a packaged, scoped milestone | work merged to `{{branches.queue}}` | prod, verified |

A fourth option, **Default**, carries no role. It is for questions, one-off fixes and exploration. The hard rules in
CLAUDE.md still bind it.

### The rule that matters most

> **File issues freely - everyone. Assign milestones - Discovery only, after reading the whole board.**

Filing is local and cheap. Assignment needs the whole board. One exception: Release files a release-*blocking* defect it
observed onto the milestone in flight.

### File forward, never sideways

A Development agent **will** find bugs. Good: write them down. But:

> File the issue with **no milestone**, labeled **`{{tracker.backlog_label}}`**. Let Discovery place it. Never add it to
> the milestone you are working.

The `{{tracker.backlog_label}}` label is the standing queue of triaged but unscheduled work
(`is:open label:{{tracker.backlog_label}}`). Anyone filing a homeless issue adds it. Discovery removes it when the issue
goes into a milestone.

**Two exceptions:**

- **A missed site of the milestone's own defect is in scope.** If the finding makes the milestone's headline or an
  invariant false, Development fixes it in the milestone. When that is close, Discovery rules.
- **Something that jeopardises the release itself** (an invariant that cannot hold, a migration that cannot work as
  specified) is a broken plan, not a scope change. Escalate; do not absorb.

**A milestone is frozen once it enters development.** A hotfix is **its own small milestone that jumps the queue**,
never an insertion into something in flight.

## The lanes

{{#if (eq release.topology "diverged-branch")}}
```
{{branches.work}} --PR--> {{branches.queue}} --promote--> {{branches.main}} --cutover merge--> {{branches.release}}
```
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq release.topology "ff-branch")}}
```
{{branches.work}} --PR--> {{branches.queue}} --promote--> {{branches.main}} --fast-forward--> {{branches.release}}
```
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq release.topology "tag")}}
```
{{branches.work}} --PR--> {{branches.queue}} --promote--> {{branches.main}} --tag {{release.tag}}--> prod
```
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq release.topology "dispatch")}}
```
{{branches.work}} --PR--> {{branches.queue}} --promote--> {{branches.main}} --dispatch--> prod
```
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq release.topology "main")}}
```
{{branches.work}} --PR--> {{branches.queue}} --promote--> {{branches.main}} (prod)
```
{{/if}}

- Development owns the work branch and the merge into the queue branch. Release owns every hop after it.
{{#if environments.lower}}
- **Environments**, in promotion order: {{#each environments.lower}}`{{this}}` -> {{/each}}`{{environments.prod}}`.
  How the lower ones receive code: {{environments.lower_deploy}}
{{/if}}
- **Prod** (`{{environments.prod}}`): {{release.prod_deploy}}
{{#if release.prod_lanes}}

### Why order is mechanism, not convention

{{#if (eq release.topology "diverged-branch")}}
`{{branches.release}}` is a **diverged branch, not a pointer into `{{branches.main}}`'s line**. It carries merge
commits `{{branches.main}}` does not. A **two-parent cutover merge** of `{{branches.main}}` advances it; a
fast-forward push fails. A cutover merges `{{branches.main}}` **wholesale**.

> **Rehearse every cutover before pushing it.** Merge `{{branches.main}}` onto a throwaway branch, then diff the merged
> tree against `{{branches.main}}`'s. Require byte-identity, or a written explanation naming every surviving file. A
> diverged branch can carry stale lines that `{{branches.main}}` does not have, and nothing else gives a reason to look.
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq release.topology "ff-branch")}}
`{{branches.release}}` is fast-forwarded to a commit on `{{branches.main}}`. It can ship a prefix of
`{{branches.main}}`, never a subset.
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq release.topology "tag")}}
Prod deploys a tag on `{{branches.main}}`. A tag ships every commit before it.
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq release.topology "dispatch")}}
Prod deploys `{{branches.main}}`'s tip when Release dispatches the prod workflow. A dispatch names a branch, not a
commit, so Release confirms `origin/{{branches.main}}` equals the verified SHA before it dispatches.
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq release.topology "main")}}
Every push to `{{branches.main}}` deploys prod. The promotion is the release.
{{/if}}

So if a later milestone lands on `{{branches.main}}` before an earlier one, **no release exists that takes the earlier
one without the later.** The queue-branch layer exists so a milestone arrives on `{{branches.main}}` as **one
promotion**. Two releases then cannot interleave, even by accident. The bad state is unrepresentable rather than
merely discouraged.

### Do not bundle the release

Bundling is expensive in a specific way: a release is **as risky as its worst member**, and its rollback and bisect
surface are the **union** of everything in it.
{{#unless (eq release.topology "main")}}

Batch the deploy instead: several finished milestones can ship in **one release window**. Separate milestones plus
one train gives the coordination benefit of a big release without its cost.
{{/unless}}

### Sizing test

> **One story, one rollback decision.** If the runbook needs two "Context" sections, it is two releases.

Bundle only what must ship together to be **correct** (a genuine atomic invariant). Never bundle what is merely
thematically similar. **Category is not coupling.** Two things that share a directory but no file are not coupled.

### Queue-branch hygiene

- No shared environment deploys from a queue branch. Keep queue branches short-lived.
- **After any promotion to `{{branches.main}}`, merge `{{branches.main}}` into every open queue branch.** Skipped, this
  drifts silently.

## Milestone descriptions carry their own boundary

Every milestone description states its edges, so a session that *stumbles onto it* can read the boundary instead of
inferring one:

```
<ONE-LINE STORY>. Runbook: {{paths.runbook_dir}}/{{paths.runbook_file}}. Umbrella: #NNN.

IN SCOPE - ...
OUT OF SCOPE - ... (and where those things go instead)
BELONGS ELSEWHERE - found a bug that breaks no line of this contract? FILE IT FORWARD: open an
  issue with NO milestone, labeled `{{tracker.backlog_label}}`, and let Discovery place it. A site of THIS
  milestone's own defect that IN SCOPE did not list is in scope: fix it here. This milestone is FROZEN.
<atomic invariants, if any>
```

The runbook template is `{{paths.runbook_dir}}/TEMPLATE-release-runbook.md`.

## Sessions and the board

{{#if coordination.desktop_session_tools}}
Sessions can see each other. Use it:

- `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__list_sessions` - who else exists, on what branch, last active when.
- `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__search_session_transcripts` - full-text search across other sessions' transcripts. Read
  what another session decided *before* deciding.
- `mcp__ccd_session_mgmt__send_message` - lands as a user turn in the target session. For handoffs and relays, not
  orchestration.

Sessions are not live between turns, so this is asynchronous: **read the board, leave a note.** The real coordination
point is GitHub: the milestone is the shared state.

- A session cannot rename itself. Its role shows as `@<role>` in the session list, and its milestone shows in its
  branch name. Both are visible to any session that lists the board.
- A terminal session does not have these tools. It reads `gh pr list --state open` and the umbrella issue's
  comments instead, and leaves its decisions as issue comments.
{{else}}
Sessions on this project cannot see each other's transcripts. **GitHub is the board.**

- **Who is working where:** `gh pr list --state open` and the recent remote branches.
- **Claims:** a session that starts milestone work comments `WORKING: <role> on <branch>` on the umbrella issue, and
  `DONE: <role>, <outcome>` when it stops.
- **Decisions:** every ruling (scope call, deferral, exception) is an issue comment. A decision that exists only in a
  transcript does not exist for the next session.
{{/if}}

## Verification standard

Applies to every role.

- **A green build is not verification.** Neither is a code-path argument.
- **Verify the artifact that ships, not the source tree.** Fetch what the client actually receives; confirm the
  running process is built from the branch you think it is.
- **Absence of an error proves nothing** where code swallows exceptions. Observe the expected *effect*: a row that
  actually changed, a value that is actually non-zero.
- **A canary can pass while every customer breaks.** Choose production-shaped fixtures.
- **When a check comes back clean, confirm you checked the thing that executes.** A search that returns nothing from
  the wrong path, a version read from the wrong install, a query against a retired resource: each reads exactly like
  a real absence.
{{#each verification.traps}}
- {{this}}
{{/each}}
- **State what you did not verify.** An honest gap is fine; an implied verification is not.

## How schema reaches an environment

- A migration script lives in `{{database.migrations_dir}}`.
{{#if database.base_schema_dir}}
- `{{database.base_schema_dir}}` holds the base-schema definitions. Keep them true when a change alters a base
  definition.
{{/if}}
{{#if (eq database.applied_by "deploy")}}
- A migration reaches an environment when that environment's deploy runs. The runbook lists each migration, says
  whether it can be reversed, and verifies the schema in each environment.
{{else}}
- A migration reaches an environment **only** through a step in its release runbook, run once per environment.
{{/if}}
- How a migration is applied: {{database.apply}}
- A lower environment that missed a deploy or a runbook step stays behind. When a gate depends on a constraint or an index, check
  it exists in the gate's environment before trusting a pass there.
{{/if}}
